# NEAR Books

<!-- summary:begin (generated by `make readme`) -->
NEAR Books rebuilds NEAR Intents' revenue, buyback and issuance numbers from raw chain data and checks 17 findings against DefiLlama and published figures, offline, with `make verify`.
A NEAR testnet contract stores attested daily snapshots of NEAR mainnet (read by a pinned worker inside OutLayer's Intel TDX enclave) and resolves dated predictions from them only: 1 snapshot(s), 7 predictions (7 pending) as of block 273,970,467.
A dashboard and an MCP server read that contract live; 143 tests (49 Python, 81 contract, 13 worker). Testnet only.
<!-- summary:end -->

## What you can verify in 2 minutes

Requirements: `python3` >= 3.10 (standard library only) and `make`. No keys, accounts or environment variables. Rust is needed only to build the contract and worker.

**1. Recompute every finding offline** (`make verify`, about 3 s). Expect every line to say PASS. The last line says the README's generated numbers and any local builds match the committed data and `contract/deployment.json`.

**4. Open the dashboard** (`make site`, then http://127.0.0.1:8000/site/). The page reads the snapshots, predictions and pin history from the testnet contract in the browser. A snapshot is marked **verified** only if all of these hold:
- its worker hash is in `contract/known_workers.json`,
- that hash is the contract's pin for that date,
- OutLayer's attestation matches the snapshot's wasm, input and output hashes,
- the attested transaction called this contract.

Without RPC access the page shows an "offline data" badge and the committed copy. Pipeline numbers carry a separate "pipeline · snapshot 2026-10-20" tag. A headless Chromium run of `tests/browser_check.mjs`:

## Architecture

```
 NEAR mainnet (archival RPC)                 FastNear transfers API, DefiLlama
        │                                              │
        │                       pipeline/fetch*.py ────┘──> data/snapshot-*/ (raw, hashed in manifest.json)
        │                                              │
        │                       pipeline/compute.py ──> metrics.json ──> verify.py (findings) ──> README tables
        │                                                    │
        │                                                    └──> site/ "pipeline · historical", mcp list_predictions
        │
        │  first block of D and of D-28 (worker checks both)
        ▼
 OutLayer TDX worker  (worker/, wasm32-wasip2, sha256 pinned in the contract and listed in contract/known_workers.json)
        ▲ request_execution(input = nonce, D, B, B28)        │ output bytes (yield/resume)
        │                                                    ▼
 anyone ── request_snapshot(D, B, B28) + 0.03 NEAR ──> nearbooks contract (NEAR testnet)
                                                      ├─ attested series: one snapshot per date, first valid wins
                                                      ├─ predictions: owner registers (future date only), anyone resolves
                                                      │    decided only by the attested snapshot of resolve_after; metric absent -> void
                                                      └─ pin history: propose_pin -> wait pin_delay_secs -> apply_pin;
                                                           a pin governs only dates starting after it is applied
        public attestation (TDX quote, wasm/input/output hashes)
                 │
                 ├──> contract/scripts/verify_attestation.py (quote binding, measurements, Intel DCAP)
                 └──> site/index.html and mcp/server.py (live view calls; hash, pin, worker-list and tx checks)
```

Each attested snapshot stores mainnet numbers at the first block of a UTC day and at the first block 28 days earlier:
- total supply,
- the three Intents revenue wallets,
- an `intents.near` reserves check,
- derived values: net issuance per day, and how much NEAR the revenue wallets kept as a share of the new supply.

The contract computes the derived values from the raw values the worker printed. Details and the chain of custody: `docs/attestation.md`.

### Predictions

The claims are dated and falsifiable, and there are no stakes. P1-P4 come from `pipeline/predictions.json`. P4 used to be "break-even volume above 2x current volume", which needs off-chain volume data. It is now the same inequality measured on-chain: break-even volume / current volume = new supply / NEAR captured. The three demo predictions resolve on the day after registration, one for each outcome (`contract/scripts/demo_predictions.json`).

| ID | Claim | Rule | Decided by the attested snapshot of | Status | Observed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 (P1) | Total NEAR supply at the first mainnet block of 2026-12-31 is higher than at the as-of snapshot (no net burn at the protocol level). | `supply_total_near > 1,309,454,857` | 2026-12-31 | **pending** | - |
| 1 (P2) | The buyback wallet holds at least as much NEAR at the first block of 2026-12-31 as at the as-of snapshot (revenue is accumulated, not spent or burned from it). | `buyback_wallet_near >= 2,024,302` | 2026-12-31 | **pending** | - |
| 2 (P3) | Net issuance over the 28 days to the first block of 2027-01-31 is still positive (total supply grew). | `net_issuance_near_per_day > 0.000` | 2027-01-31 | **pending** | - |
| 3 (P4) | In the 28 days to the first block of 2027-01-31 the three Intents revenue wallets gain less than half as much NEAR as total supply grows (burning all revenue would offset under 50% of issuance). | `revenue_wallets_gain_over_net_issuance < 0.500` | 2027-01-31 | **pending** | - |

| 6 (demo) | Volume needed for net deflation exceeds 2x current volume at the first block of the resolve date (the old P4 metric, which the worker does not compute; expected void). | `breakeven_over_current_volume > 2.000` | 2026-10-21 | **pending** | - |

After that snapshot is attested and `resolve_prediction` has been called, the outcome of each demo (expected confirmed, refuted and void) will be recorded in the table above and in `contract/testnet-resolve.log`.

## Trust assumptions and limits

- **RPC data.** The worker reads NEAR mainnet over HTTPS JSON-RPC (archival FastNear, fallback `rpc.mainnet.near.org`) without state proofs. `evidence_hash` commits to the raw responses. A local `wasmtime` run of the pinned worker against the same endpoint reproduced the 2026-10-20 evidence hash (`875a2965…7ec0`).
- **The quote is checked off-chain.** The contract only knows that the bytes came back from the configured OutLayer contract, for a run of the pinned hash, answering this request's nonce and blocks. The TDX quote, its binding to the run and Intel's signature chain are checked by `verify_attestation.py`. The dashboard and MCP server check the hashes, the pin and the transaction, but not the quote.
- **Owner powers.** The owner is the contract account. It can:
  - register predictions (future dates only; never edit, delete or resolve them),
  - rotate the reporter (whose snapshots never decide anything),
  - move `earliest_date` earlier,
  - propose, apply or cancel re-pins (timelocked, 1 h on testnet),
  - transfer ownership.

  It cannot write or alter attested snapshots, and it cannot move requesters' funds. **It can still redeploy the code with the account's full-access key, which bypasses every rule above.** A mainnet deployment would use a timelock of days, and it would delete the full-access key after deploying (locking the code) or hand ownership to a multisig with `transfer_ownership`. Neither was done; this is a testnet prototype. Full table: `docs/attestation.md`.
- **Builds.** The worker builds byte-identically from another directory with the same toolchain. The contract is a `cargo near build non-reproducible-wasm` build, so a different rustc or cargo-near can give a different hash. `make verify` reports a local build that differs from `contract/deployment.json`.
- **Metric definitions.** "Revenue wallets kept" is the change in the three wallets' balances. Their spending reduces it, and internal transfers between them cancel out. The pipeline's transfer-based estimate for the same window (17.2%) agrees with the attested balance-based value (17.5%). Only native NEAR counts.
- **Pipeline limits.** F1 is a consistency check against DefiLlama, which uses the same wallets, so it is not independent proof. The break-even model is deliberately simple. Some published figures were typed in by hand from pages that render client-side. More in `docs/findings.md`.
- **Dashboard and MCP.** They trust the testnet RPC they read, and the dashboard reads only the contract hard-coded in it. They fetch only allowlisted HTTPS origins (testnet RPCs, archival testnet RPCs for transactions, and OutLayer's attestation API). Redirects are refused. Attestation URLs are rebuilt from the numeric request id rather than taken from contract state.
- **Testnet only.** Nothing was deployed to mainnet and no mainnet funds were used.

## Repository layout

```
pipeline/   fetch.py fetch_m2.py compute.py verify.py report.py readme_facts.py update_readme.py config.json predictions.json
data/       snapshot-2026-10-20/ snapshot-2026-10-20-m2/   committed raw inputs + manifest.json + metrics.json
contract/   src/{lib.rs,tests.rs}  deployment.json  known_workers.json  testnet-*.log
            scripts/{testnet_attested.sh,testnet_resolve.sh,verify_attestation.py,check_deployment.py,make_args.py,demo_predictions.json}
worker/     src/{lib.rs,main.rs,tests.rs}  build.sh  scripts/{first_block.py,rank_intents_tokens.py}
mcp/        server.py (MCP over stdio)  chain.py (testnet view calls, offline cache)
site/       index.html  metrics.json  contract-cache.json  screenshot.png
docs/       attestation.md  findings.md
tests/      test_pipeline.py  test_mcp.py  browser_check.mjs (optional, needs node + playwright-core)
```

MCP client setup: `claude mcp add nearbooks -- python3 /path/to/nearbooks/mcp/server.py`. Tools: `get_attested_snapshots`, `get_predictions`, `get_contract_config` (live), `get_metrics`, `get_reconciliation`, `list_predictions` (pipeline).
